I think for us people away from the action, it may not be clear how ridiculously fast astro-tech is evolving.

  • 1950s - most people still thought Venus was probably a planet with a tropical climate that might even habor advanced animal life.
  • 1957 - Sputnik 1, the first probe humanity launched into space ever.
  • 1969 - humans land on the moon, NASA's funding begins to disappear.
  • 1971 - NASA funds a SETI study culminating in the recommendation of the development of a type of telescope. The government refuses to fund this and continues slashing NASA's budget.
  • 1975 - first probes to land on Mars.
  • Around here NASA had had about 80% of their budgetary share cut - their reward for winning the space race. Many plans were proposed, cut, and defunded, repeatedly. One can only imagine where we'd be today if we'd chose to have kept NASA funded.
  • 1977 - the "WOW!" signal, a still unexplained strong radio signal from a distant galaxy was received.
  • 1980 - privately funded searches for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) begin to develop.
  • 1981 - following lobbying by a senator determined to further defund NASA, congress decided to remove all SETI funding. It would be refunded about a year later, but it's indicative of the issues at play.
  • 1992 - NASA finally receives funding to begin an operational SETI program known as the microwave observing program or MOP. It was intended to be a longterm widescale observation of the sky along with specific searches carried out in certain locations.
  • 1992 - ... yes the same year. congress literally ridicules NASA searching for extraterrestrial life and completely cancels the longterm MOP SETI program.
  • 1995 - first discovery of a planetary body orbiting another star. it was a massive jupiter-like planet because that's all we could find at the time
  • 2005 - first probe landed on a moon of Saturn. Carl Sagan spoke passionately of this one, but didn't live to see it.
  • 2009 - we discovered widespread water on the moon - think about how recent this discovery is. this was also a game changer. moon colonies before were difficult to justify. water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen which can be used to produce rocket fuel. another little reminder that we don't know what we don't know when it comes to reasons to explore and habitate other locations.
  • 2009 - Kepler telescope is launched to help discover earth-like bodies orbiting other stars
  • 2014 - thanks to Kepler, NASA announces 715 verified exoplanets, many of them earth-like.
  • 2016 - again thanks to Kepler, NASA announces 1,284 more confirmed exoplanets, again many earth-like planets among them.

I am leaving a ton out here, but hopefully it can give a feel for how quickly things are improving. It might also give you a feel for how much our government has worked to handicap space technology in the United states. But even in spite of that we've been having rapidly accelerating progress. The huge increase in information is because of a huge increase in information. There has also been a sharp rise in private funding which is excellent since it means the funding is not contingent on the whims of geriatric technically and scientifically illiterate career politicians. We'd never have landed on the moon if not for government funding, but we'd have been on Mars decades ago if not for government myopia.
